title: Corrigendum to “Two-Year Outcome of Aflibercept in Patients with Pigment Epithelial Detachment due to Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration (nAMD) Refractory to Ranibizumab”

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

condition: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration with pigment epithelial detachment refractory to ranibizumab, switched to aflibercept; corrected Table 2 (time of switch to 24 months) published as a corrigendum to the original article doi:10.1155/2017/8984313 (PMC5615945), whose Methods are not part of this source

groups.agent: intravitreal aflibercept (dose and schedule not given in the corrigendum)
groups.description: Eyes switched from ranibizumab to aflibercept

exclusions.reason: macular volume is out of scope

exclusions.what: Corrected Table 2 subfoveal choroidal thickness row (R7)
exclusions.reason: choroidal thickness is out of scope

exclusions.what: Corrected Table 2 P columns (C4, C6, C8, C10)
Corrected Results sentence with CRT values
exclusions.reason: duplicates the corrected table; the table is cited

notes: Same cohort as the original article doi:10.1155/2017/8984313 (PMC5615945); linked here so the cohort is not entered twice. The corrigendum's corrected table supersedes the original Table 2.

Ambiguity resolved: the corrigendum contains no Methods, so the thickness definition, OCT device and aflibercept regimen are recorded as central_unspecified, unstated and unstated; the original article was not used as a source.
Ambiguity resolved: the N row sits under a row-spanned header; its five cells map to the Baseline, Month 3, Month 6, Month 12 and Month 24 columns.

series.baseline_label: Baseline at the time of switch (corrected Table 2, central macular thickness row, column 2)
series.notes: mean ± SD (table footnote); baseline = time of switch to aflibercept; N row (R2) gives 44 eyes at baseline and months 3, 6 and 12 and 38 at month 24 (attrition); handling of missing visits not stated
